cohort: 272,472 live, singleton, term births without congenital anomalies recorded in the Malaysian National Obstetrics Registry between 2010 and 2012, of which 1,580 (0.59%) had 1-minute Apgar scores <4.
finding: Only 29.4% of neonates with 1-minute Apgar scores <4 recovered to a 5-minute Apgar score >=7, with delivery by a doctor, planned or unplanned cesarean section, maternal obesity, and certain ethnicities being associated with higher odds of recovery.
mod_finding: Among deliveries by doctors, planned and unplanned cesarean section was associated with better odds of recovery than uncomplicated vaginal deliveries.
